newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition declines despite rains.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition declines despite rains.

text.p: The Texas wheat crop condition declined slightly in the week to Sunday despite beneficial rains in the High Plains, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said Monday in its weekly crop report.
Wheat was rated 51 percent good to excellent, down from 55 percent a week earlier.
"Dryland fields in the Plains benefitted from the first good rain in a while. Irrigated fields remained in good condition, the report said.
Rust and mildew problems increased with the wet conditions.
Statewide wheat condition was rated at 73 percent of normal compared with 35 percent last year.
Corn planting was getting under way early in the week in some fields in the High Plains when rainfall stalled progress. Fina planting operations were delayed in central areas.
Corn was 40 percent planted, down from 51 percent last year and a five-year average of 46 percent. It was rated 35 percent good to excellent.
Ranges and pastures were rated 14 percent excellent, 32 good, 38 fair, 12 poor and four very poor.
